experiment: P5h exclusive-GPU guarded shared frozen-forward and dense bounded-head execution
research_question: Can the unchanged P5g shared-one-forward, dense-head execution obtain exact frozen P5e outputs and a measured latency reduction when the cost protocol enforces no concurrent Python experimental process before, during and after every CUDA-synchronized warmup and timed repeat?
single_changed_axis: P5g execution mechanism is unchanged; P5h adds only an exclusive-device guard to make the cost measurement interpretable after P5g's concurrent-GPU execution freeze.

execution.reference: two frozen base forwards plus unchanged dense attachment
execution.candidate: one frozen base forward plus identical unchanged dense attachment
execution.timing: CUDA synchronize before and after each run; external Python process guard before and after every warmup/repeat; record GPU snapshot

development_data.roles: evaluation-only; no training, selection, calibration or threshold adjustment

stop_rule: Any external Python process at preflight or a guard checkpoint stops the run before a result is written; the accessed P5h pool is then frozen and cannot be rerun. Any equivalence or latency failure stops P5h with no threshold, head, weight, feature, batch, scheduling, compiler or quantization change and no confirmation.

confirmation_if_and_only_if_development_.decision: Only a pass supports a narrow frozen-execution cost claim, never a new architecture or classification claim.
